forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: i7 Cabinet 120826 2026-27 Month 2 Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Community Equipment Service cost pressure of £0.96m due to previous contractor insolvency, requiring recommissioning with partners
findings.detail: Integration and Partnerships directorate is overspending by £1.0m, mainly from Community Equipment costs of £0.96m. The paper states 'Higher costs for delivery of service due to the insolvency of the previous contracted provider. The service is to be recommissioned in collaboration with partners across South Yorkshire.' This is a one-off spike, but recommissioning risk remains.
findings.matters: Contractor insolvency forced emergency service continuity, pushing costs up. This is unplanned spending that reveals supply chain fragility in a critical adult care support service. Recommissioning introduces execution and budget risk.
findings.figures: Integration and Partnerships £1.0m overspend; Community Equipment £0.96m of that
findings.quote: Integration and Partnerships: £1.00m overspend, primarily driven by £0.96m pressure in Community Equipment. Higher costs for delivery of service due to the insolvency of the previous contracted provider. The service is to be recommissioned in collaboration with partners across South Yorkshire

findings.paper_title: i7 Cabinet 120826 2026-27 Month 2 Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Commercial estate income under pressure from NCP insolvency (£0.34m), Colonnades empty units (£0.28m) and town centre tenant defaults (£0.18m)
findings.detail: NCP car park operator insolvency is costing £0.34m in lost income; Colonnades Shopping Centre empty units forcing council to cover NNDR costs of £0.28m; Herten Triangle (TGI Fridays, Estabulo closures) costing £0.18m as administrators recover properties; general town centre portfolio income pressure with 'no formal plan in place to deal with this owing to difficult market conditions which is making tenants for the portfolio harder to find.'
findings.matters: These are revenue income lines, and multiple properties are in distress simultaneously. 'No formal plan' for a £0.20m+ income pressure signals either limited levers to pull or strategic decisions deferred. For lenders, it suggests the commercial estate strategy is under stress and property values/income may be deteriorating.
findings.figures: NCP overspend £0.34m; Colonnades £0.28m; Herten Triangle £0.18m; CCQ service charges £0.11m; total Strategic Asset Management overspend £1.21m
findings.quote: Collapse of NCP – overspend of £0.34m due to under achievement of income...Colonnades Shopping Centre – overspend of £0.28m due to additional NNDR costs...currently there is no formal plan in place to deal with this owing to difficult market conditions which is making tenants for the portfolio harder to find

findings.paper_title: i7 Cabinet 120826 2026-27 Month 2 Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: DSG cumulative deficit forecast at £80m (2026/27) rising to £122.7m (2027/28), with out-of-authority placements rising from 230 to 323 projected by March 2027
findings.detail: Doncaster faces an £80m cumulative DSG deficit by end of 2026/27 (forecast to reach £122.7m by 2027/28). Out-of-authority SEND placements are rising sharply: 217 at April 2026, 230 now, projected to 323 by March 2027. Government has committed to funding 90% via High Needs Stability Grant (90% of historic deficit, 90% of in-year deficits), but only if council produces 'satisfactory SEND reform plan.' The statutory override protecting councils from the deficit ends March 2028, when the council becomes liable for 10% (~£12.3m). If DfE funding drops to 75%, council liability rises to £23m.
findings.matters: This is a structural liability with a cliff edge. A £12-23m liability hitting the general fund in 2028 would require either massive reserves, cuts elsewhere, or borrowing. For lenders, it reveals latent liabilities and dependency on government relief that may not materialise. The reform plan condition adds execution risk.
findings.figures: £80m cumulative DSG deficit 2026/27; £122.7m projected 2027/28; out-of-authority placements 217→230→323 (projected); revised cumulative balance after 90% DfE funding £8m 2026/27, £12.3m council liability over 3 years; 75% funding scenario: £23m council liability; override ends 31 March 2028
findings.quote: cumulative overspend on DSG of £80.0m at 31 March 2027...The total placement numbers were 217 at 1st April 2026 and are currently 230, then projected to rise further to 323 by 31st March 2027...Should DfE funding reduce to, say, 75% in 2026/27 and 2027/28, the Council would need to find £23.0m in total

findings.paper_title: i7 Cabinet 120826 2026-27 Month 2 Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Green Waste savings of £0.81m unachievable despite being approved in budget-setting, creating Waste directorate overspend
findings.detail: The council budgeted for £0.81m Green Waste income/savings improvement. The paper states this 'was proposed at budget setting but has subsequently proved to be unachievable.' Collection overspend also includes higher than expected domestic collection costs from 'more properties being collected from than were budgeted for.'
findings.matters: Failed savings indicate either budget planning detachment from operational reality or execution weakness. £0.81m is material; if savings assumptions are failing this early and this confidently, questions arise about other approved savings hitting their targets.
findings.figures: Green Waste planned savings £0.81m; Waste total overspend £1.24m; Collection overspend £1.09m
findings.quote: The biggest forecast variance is on Collection, which is forecasting an overspend of £1.09m which is mainly due to a Green Waste pressure of £0.81m, which was proposed at budget setting but has subsequently proved to be unachievable

findings.paper_title: i7 Cabinet 120826 2026-27 Month 2 Financial Monitoring Report
findings.headline: Adult Social Care demand outrunning budget by £2.5m-£3.56m, driven by higher residential care placements and homecare unit costs
findings.detail: Residential care overspends £1.93m due to 718 older people (vs 701 budgeted, costing £0.79m) and 625 extra short-stay days per month. Homecare unit cost is £1,765 actual vs £1,571 budgeted — 12% above plan — driving a £1.12m overspend. These are demand-driven and difficult to reverse mid-year.
findings.matters: Adult care is both structural (demographic) and volatile. A £2.5m+ overspend in Month 2 of a service that serves vulnerable people signals either policy/demographic shift or budget planning failure. Both matter to lenders: unplanned spending risks reserves, and if driven by demographics, it signals recurring pressure.
findings.figures: Older people residential: 718 clients vs 701 budgeted (£0.79m overspend); homecare unit cost £1,765 vs £1,571 budgeted; short-stay additional days ~625/month (£0.47m overspend); total Adults directorate overspend £3.56m
findings.quote: Residential care is projected to overspend by £1.93m, made up of: Older People Residential Care: £1.46m overspend...£0.79m due to higher starting client numbers (718 compared to 701 budgeted)...Homecare: £1.12m overspend, reflecting increased average cost (the budget is £1,571 whereas month 2 is £1,765, this will be subject to further review)
